standard_prerequisites.name: The question of openness and closedness of a subset of the target being local on the target, and quasi-compactness of the source over an affine base
standard_prerequisites.use: Permits replacing the base by an affine open and covering the quasi-compact source by finitely many affine opens, including after replacing the source by their disjoint union.

standard_prerequisites.name: Generalizations lift along flat morphisms, cited from the same chapter, and the topological lemma that images of sets stable under generalization are the complements of sets stable under specialization
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the complement of the candidate closed subset is stable under generalization, hence the subset itself is stable under specialization.

standard_prerequisites.name: The algebra lemma that a subset of an affine scheme stable under specialization is closed
standard_prerequisites.use: Closes the affine case of the argument, from which the general case follows by the initial reductions.

core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case: the question is local on the target, so take an affine base, then cover the quasi-compact source by finitely many affine opens and replace it by their disjoint union, which is again affine with a surjective flat map to the base and has the same preimages of subsets, so both source and target may be assumed affine (proof lines 3072-3080).

Set up the closed case in the affine situation: for a surjective flat ring map A to B and a subset T with closed preimage equal to the closed subscheme defined by an ideal J of B, use surjectivity to identify T with the image of the spectrum of B modulo J in the spectrum of A (proof lines 3082-3087).

Conclude closedness: since generalizations lift along the flat map, the topological lemma shows that the complement of T, being the image of the complement of the preimage, is stable under generalization, so T is stable under specialization, and the algebra lemma makes T closed (proof lines 3088-3095).
Recover the open case by applying the closed case to complements, which is the resp. clause of the statement (proof lines 3072 and 3095).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a surjective flat morphism of affine schemes by locality on the target and by replacing the quasi-compact source by the disjoint union of finitely many affine opens (proof lines 3072-3080).

For a subset with closed preimage, exhibit it as the image of a closed subscheme, show its complement is stable under generalization via lifting of generalizations, and conclude closedness by the affine criterion (proof lines 3082-3095).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a quasi-compact, surjective and flat morphism detects open and closed subsets on the source: a subset of the target is open, respectively closed, exactly when its preimage is, so the morphism is submersive (statement lines 5060-5070). The counted proof reduces first by locality on the target and by replacing the quasi-compact source with the disjoint union of finitely many affine opens, then handles the affine case by writing a subset with closed preimage as the image of a closed subscheme, using that generalizations lift along the flat map to get that its complement is stable under generalization, and applying the affine criterion that specialization-stable subsets are closed (proof lines 3072-3095). It is H2: the argument is a complete reduction chain carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard topological and algebraic criteria.
